Definition: Chananel, probably an Israelite, from whom a tower of Jerusalem was named
BiblicalUsage: Hananeel is not a man but a tower, the tower of Jerusalem that marks the city's edges in promise and in rebuilding. Jeremiah says the city shall be built to the LORD from the tower of Hananeel to the gate of the corner, Eliashib the priest built from the sheep gate even to the tower of Hananeel, and Zechariah sees the city lifted up from Benjamin's gate to the tower of Hananeel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a tower named God has favoured is the right landmark for a city God promised to rebuild. The same tower appears in the promise, in the rebuilding, and in the last vision, and I hold that God finishes what He measures out.
